messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a quick‑start playbook for getting your acoustic guitar sold—whether you’re looking for a quick cash deal, a fair trade‑in, or a higher‑priced sale on a specialty site. | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |------|------------|----------------|------| | **1. Clean & Prep** | Give the guitar a thorough wipe‑down, polish the finish, and tighten loose strings. | A pristine instrument looks more valuable and reduces buyer hesitation. | Use a microfiber cloth, a mild cleaner (or a dedicated guitar polish), and a soft brush for the fretboard. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture front, back, side, headstock, bridge, and any unique features or flaws. | Visuals drive interest; buyers rarely visit in person. | Shoot in natural light, use a plain background, and zoom in on details. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, and local classifieds. | Sets a realistic price and helps you negotiate confidently. | Look at similar models, age, condition, and any extras (case, strap). | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, condition, any upgrades, and a short story. | Transparency builds trust and reduces back‑and‑forth. | Use bullet points, keep it concise, and highlight what makes yours special. | | **5. Choose Your Platform(s)** | • **Reverb** – great for gear enthusiasts.
• **eBay** – broad audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist/Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local music shops** – consignment or direct purchase. | Different platforms reach different buyers. | If you’re in a city with a strong music scene, consider a local shop or a community group. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point can still land you a good deal. | Factor in shipping costs if you’ll ship. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | • **Shipping** – use a sturdy case, bubble wrap, and insured freight.
• **Pickup** – safer, no shipping fees. | Shipping expands your market but adds risk; pickup keeps it simple. | Offer both options if possible. | | **8. Handle Payment Securely** | • **PayPal** – buyer protection.
• **Escrow services** (for high‑value items).
• **Cash** – only if meeting in person. | Protects against fraud and ensures you get paid. | Never accept personal checks unless you’ve verified them. | | **9. Close the Sale** | Confirm payment, ship or arrange pickup, and provide a receipt. | A professional finish leaves a good impression and may lead to referrals. | Keep a copy of all correspondence and receipts. | | **10. Follow Up** | Ask for a review or feedback. | Positive reviews boost future listings. | Keep it polite and brief. | ### Quick Checklist - [ ] Clean & polish - [ ] Take 8–12 photos - [ ] Research comparable listings - [ ] Draft a concise description - [ ] List on 2–3 platforms - [ ] Set price + shipping terms - [ ] Secure payment method - [ ] Ship or meet safely - [ ] Request a review --- #### Extra Tips | Situation | Recommendation | |-----------|----------------| | **You’re a beginner seller** | Start on a local marketplace (Craigslist/Facebook) to avoid shipping headaches. | | **You want the best price** | List on Reverb or eBay; these sites attract serious collectors who pay premium prices. | | **You’re in a tight spot** | Offer a trade‑in at a local shop or pawn; they’ll give you instant cash. | | **Your guitar has sentimental value** | Highlight its history in the description; buyers love stories. | | **You’re worried about scams** | Use PayPal Goods & Services or an escrow service; never accept money before shipping. | Good luck! If you hit a snag—say, a buyer wants a lower price or you’re unsure about shipping—just let me know and I can help you craft a counter‑offer or find a reliable shipping partner.
